implication: no rerun-drift control is needed for Δ > 0.01 obj, and at ~1 min/run every sweep in the queue is affordable within one day — run both arms of each sweep rather than one

finding: top-10 by dividend-yield TTM alone earns nothing (annual -0.20%, maxdd 26.38%): the whole base result depends on the low-turnover rank
implication: the 股息率 claim as worded (excess from the yield end, not the turnover rank) is refuted; the open question is WHY raw top yield fails — test whether ST/distressed names (yield inflated by a collapsed price) are the trap (q-7) and whether yield only works inside the low-turnover subset (q-8)

finding: low 20d turnover among dividend payers alone gives annual 11.56% at maxdd 11.28% — positive but far below the combination; removing the yield rank costs 0.132 obj
implication: the two ranks are complementary, not additive: yield alone -0.2658, turnover alone 0.0028, both 0.1348. Improve ideas must keep BOTH ranks; the rank weights (3:3) become an on-mechanism sweep worth running (q-9)

component_or_param: ST/退/次新 filter on the yield-only book

component_or_param: yield rank inside 20d-turnover terciles (low: q-8a, high: q-8b)
finding: pure yield within the lowest-turnover tercile still falls well short of the base (-0.0663 vs 0.1348) while within the highest tercile it tracks the market crash (-0.4574); turnover level orders the results monotonically (high tercile < low tercile < rank-sum base)
description: payers split by turnover_20d tercile, top-10 by dy_rank within the tercile; two runs
implication: the conditional 股息率 claim is refuted: a coarse low-turnover screen plus max-yield is not the mechanism — the base needs names EXTREME on turnover (q-2 alone +14.26 in 2022), so turnover rank is the load-bearing leg and yield a secondary sort. Opens q-9 (rank weights) as the direct test of how much yield adds on top of turnover

finding: objective peaks at equal weights and falls ~0.08 symmetrically when either rank is tilted 3x, i.e. a single sharp peak rather than a plateau; with the full sweep endpoints q-1 (-0.2658) and q-2 (0.0028) the curve is -0.27 / 0.06 / 0.13 / 0.05 / 0.00
implication: the weight knob is closed for improve (both neighbours lose); and because 1:1 sits on a narrow peak, the base 0.1348 is likely partly an in-sample optimum — any VAL expectation should be discounted toward the 0.05 shoulder, and improve ideas must keep the 1:1 rank-sum untouched so their Δ is not a re-tune of this knob

finding: inside CSI800 the same rule keeps ~60% of the objective (annual 17.89% vs 22.61%) at an unchanged drawdown; the remaining ~0.054 comes from names outside the 800
description: get_stock_pool intersected with get_index_stocks(000906.XSHG) at each rebalance
implication: the family is not a disguised 规模因子 book, so it is NOT integration-redundant with 小市值 on edge grounds — record that for type integration; but ~40% of the objective does sit in smaller names, so an improve idea that widens the small-cap tilt would be off-mechanism drift toward the saturated size factor and should be rejected at the gate

finding: 5 and 10 names score alike (0.120 / 0.135) while widening to 20 costs 0.057 at the same drawdown: the return is concentrated in the top of the rank-sum, not spread across a broad high-yield/low-turnover sleeve
implication: closes breadth as an improve lever (widening dilutes, narrowing to 5 does not gain); together with q-8 it says the signal lives at the joint extreme, so improve ideas should sharpen the ranking inputs (better yield/turnover measures, i-1) rather than change book size

finding: shifting the 25-day rebalance calendar by 12 days changes the objective by only -0.006 with an identical drawdown
description: counter offset g.phase=12, first day still rebalances
implication: closed: the base result is not a lucky rebalance calendar, so the q-9 weight peak is the only fragility found so far and the rebalance cycle need not be re-swept by improve ideas

component_or_param: 2022 vs 2023 split of the TRAIN curves (base, q-1, q-2, q-3)
finding: the base earns about equally in both years against a falling benchmark; yield-only fails ENTIRELY in the 2022 bear (-14.31, the whole 26% drawdown) and works in 2023, while turnover-only is the better of the two in 2022
flags: curve-split, not independent re-runs (holdings carry over the year boundary)
description: stored daily curves chained within each calendar year, no backtest spent
implication: locates the turnover leg as the bear-market defence and the yield leg as the 2023 return source, so the family is not a single-regime artifact; VAL (2024-25, a strong 红利 rally) will mostly exercise the yield leg — read a VAL result as evidence about yield, not about the turnover defence

component_or_param: yield measure: TTM per-share cash dividend / price -> 3-year avg cash dividend / market cap (from 2596a8ab)
finding: replacing TTM yield with a 3-year average dividend yield cuts the objective to -0.0107, about the level of turnover-only (q-2 0.0028) — the smoothed yield adds almost nothing on top of the turnover rank
description: enhance/candidates/hlld-i-1.py, rank-sum and all else identical; rejected
implication: closed: dividend smoothing / longer lookback is the wrong direction — what the yield leg contributes is the RECENT (trailing-12m) payout, so future yield ideas should make the measure fresher (e.g. announced-not-yet-paid plans), never longer

component_or_param: earnings-quality pre-screen PE 5-50, ROE>5, net-profit YoY>0 (from 1a8a41cf)

description: enhance/candidates/hlld-i-3.py, get_fundamentals screen at previous_date; rejected
implication: closed: growth/quality filters are anti-mechanism here — the rank-sum earns on ex-growth, low-attention payers that a profit-growth screen removes, leaving cyclicals near peak earnings. Explains why member 1a8a41cf (same filters) scores only 0.0286; do not borrow 1a8a41cf's screen in any form

implication: closed: the yield-measure axis is exhausted — longer (i-1, -0.146) and earlier (i-4, -0.018) both lose, so the base TTM-by-registration measure stays; the only unswept input left is the turnover leg (q-10)

finding: 20 days is the best of the three; 60 days loses less than 10 days and has the lowest drawdown, so shortening the window hurts more than lengthening it
implication: closed as an improve knob (no arm beats 20d); the asymmetry (60d > 10d) supports reading low turnover as a persistent low-attention attribute rather than a short-term liquidity blip, which is what the 流动性溢价 claim needs — no further turnover-measure ideas are queued
